# About the Author {.unnumbered}

![Photo of Michael Borck](images/author-photo.jpg){fig-alt="Photo of Michael Borck, the author" width=200px fig-align="center"}

**Michael Borck** is a software developer and educator working at the intersection of human expertise and artificial intelligence. He teaches applied AI and AI in business at Curtin University, and runs *The Human Edge* masterclasses through Curtin Executive Education. *Build AI, Understand AI* grew out of a simple classroom observation: students could use AI tools fluently long before they could say what those tools were doing, and the gap closed fastest when they built a tiny version themselves.

His earlier book, *Conversation, Not Delegation*, argues for treating AI as a thinking partner you converse with. *Speak Software* teaches readers to direct agents without writing code. This book opens the box those agents are built on: every chapter reduces one familiar AI system to a single model call wrapped in plain Python, built in miniature so it can be read in one sitting. The doing lives in the companion package, `hands-on-ai` (`pip install hands-on-ai`), whose modules, documentation and project guides this book narrates; neither duplicates the other.

The bet underneath the book is that models change every few months and the ideas underneath them change slowly. A reader who has built chat, retrieval, an agent loop, a workflow and a judge by hand stops being fooled by demos, whatever the next model is called. Michael builds educational software and resources, and writes about the 80/20 principle in learning and professional judgement.
